findings.reason: with no node producing labels for RRF ranks 11–60, every rerank arm run raises UnlabelledCandidates and names its candidates, so §7's done-when (the rerank measured against fusion alone on the pooled labels) cannot be satisfied and a builder would have to invent the labelling step the plan omits.
findings.text: §7's added paragraph and its done-when require "their labels cover RRF's top 60 on every question rather than a top-10 union", yet §3's only labelling node (line 174, "The third pools and labels every arm's top 10") produces top-10 depth, runs before §7 (the followup orders §7 after §4, which follows §3), and §7's own text assigns the arms "to score, not to label"; the committed harness enforces exactly this through require_labelled on the rerank's top 10 (tests/llm/test_signal_search_goldens.py:193), which pulls anywhere from RRF rank 1 to rank 60

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_search_signals` (imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:272), `rerank_candidates` (imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:171), `_RERANK_QUESTION` (imas_codex/llm/search_tools.py:84), and the cited fixture and harness (tests/llm/fixtures/signal_search_questions.json, tests/llm/test_signal_search_goldens.py) all resolve at the review base.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §3's done-when names its negative control (the seeded random-order permutation that must score below every arm), and §7's done-when carries a falsifiable ship condition ("ships on only if … otherwise it ships off") measured beside the generic-question and fusion-alone arms.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §3's table and labelling log land on the repository path docs/evidence/fragments/signal-search-finds-the-measured-signal/goldens.html, and §7's rerank report is the same harness's output, not a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the changed prose of §3 and §7 introduces no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags into code and states the mechanism (pooled labelling, the arm functions run outside pytest) rather than a tracker reference.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §7's new paragraph requires the arms' labels to cover RRF's top 60, but the only labelling node is §3's, which labels each arm's top 10 and runs before §7, and §7 assigns only scoring.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §3 closes on the golden harness plus pooled labels; §7 closes on the role-aware rerank's ship decision; the change moved scoring of the two Jev arms wholly to §7 rather than leaving §3 carrying two deliverables.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §3's arm list now names §7 as the owner of the two rerank arms ("plus any arm a later section adds; §7 adds the two reranks"), and the followup's ordering (§3 → §4 → §7) resolves every input each of the two changed units declares.
